text:
mina: quick sketch for adaptive tenant batching + RBAC lease idea. goal: keep small-tenant latency low while giving heavy tenants predictable throughput and avoiding RBAC cold-miss storms

raf: what do you mean by lease? sounds interesting

mina: lease = short-lived pin in the access cache. executor can request a lease for a tenant's policy for N seconds (renewable). while leased, shim will serve reads without remote lookups and avoid blocking on fetches. when not leased, shim behaves as normal LRU cache

jordan: tradeoffs? sounds like extra state and potential staleness on policy change

mina: yes. mitigations: leases are conservative (default 30s), policy-change webhook invalidates active leases immediately, and we keep a fast revocation channel from policy store -> console control plane -> executors

yun: how does batching tie in?

mina: two pieces:
1) per-tenant adaptive batch windows: small tenants get 4ms headway, heavy tenants get a longer window (up to 20ms) but larger batch capacity. the executor computes a moving average of request rate and switches window.
2) when tenant is leased, executor can be more aggressive with batching (larger max_batch_size) because RBAC checks are local and cheap

raf: config example pls

mina: snippet:
```
console.adaptive_batching = {
  default_headway_ms: 4,
  max_headway_ms: 20,
  headway_scale_threshold_rps: 50,
  base_max_batch: 32,
  leased_max_batch: 128,
}
console.rbac_lease = {
  default_ttl_sec: 30,
  max_ttl_sec: 120,
  eviction_on_update: true,
  lease_cost_budget: 1000, # max concurrent leases per region
}
```

jordan: sounds promising. need safety valves: 1) limit total leased tenants per executor (lease_cost_budget), 2) cap queue depth to avoid head-of-line blocking, 3) fail-open vs fail-closed policy on lease expiry

yun: ops side: add metrics lease_acquired, lease_revoked, lease_expired, lease_conflicts, batch_size_by_tenant, headway_ms_by_tenant. alerts: lease_conflicts > 1% and p99 latency delta > 5%

mina: rollout idea: start with simulation in test harness (mixed-tenant), then small internal canary with leases disabled (verify batching benefits), then enable leases for <1% of tenants behind FF console.rbac_lease.v1 and watch revocation latency under policy churn

raf: implementation owner? I can pair with mina for the executor changes, jordan can help revocation channel. yun owns telemetry and alerts. infra-bot: create feature flag and canary toggle

infra-bot: deploybot: feature-flag console.rbac_lease.v1 created by mina

mina: final notes: ensure evals include token-rotation and policy-update storms; we don't want revocation fanout to overload control plane. also add a soft-stale header for debugging: x-console-allow-stale-lease

raf: :thumbsup: let's put a doc in the RFC follow-ups and schedule a 30m sync after prototype PR

mina: will do, thanks everyone
